text: # Visitor and Attendant Guidelines
Document ID: POL-VIS-004 | Version: 1.8 | Department: Security & Operations
## 1. Visiting Hours
- General Wards: 04:00 PM – 07:00 PM daily.
- Intensive Care Units (ICU/CCU/NICU): 05:00 PM – 06:00 PM (strictly 15 minutes per visitor).
- Pediatric Ward: One resident parent/guardian permitted 24/7; general visitors 04:00 PM – 06:00 PM.
## 2. Attendant Passes
- Inpatient Rooms: Exactly one (1) 24-hour attendant pass issued per admitted patient.
- Semi-Private/General Wards: Exactly one (1) attendant pass issued.
- Passes must be worn and visible at all times within hospital premises.
## 3. General Restrictions
- Children under 12 years of age are not permitted in ICU, isolation wards, or oncology units.
- Outside cooked food, floral arrangements, and latex balloons are strictly prohibited in clinical zones.
- Photography or audio/video recording of staff, facilities, or other patients without administrative consent is strictly banned.
# Hospital Admission and Discharge Policy
Document ID: POL-ADM-001 | Version: 2.3 | Department: Administration
## 1. Admission Guidelines
1.1 Planned Admissions:
- Patients must present a signed Admission Request Form from a registered hospital consultant.
- Pre-authorization from insurance/TPA or an initial financial deposit must be secured at the front desk prior to room allocation.
- The attending nurse must complete the initial nursing assessment, vitals check, and allergy verification within 30 minutes of room arrival.
1.2 Emergency Admissions:
- Patients arriving through the Emergency Department (ED) requiring admission receive priority bed assignment regardless of financial clearance.
- Financial clearance and registration formalities must be reconciled by the family or guarantor within 12 hours of admission.
## 2. Discharge Procedures
2.1 Medical Clearance:
- Discharges must be authorized by the primary consultant before 11:00 AM to facilitate same-day room turnaround.
- The primary team must generate the Discharge Summary detailing diagnosis, hospital course, discharge medications, dietary advice, and follow-up appointment date.
2.2 Pharmacy and Billing Reconciliation:
- Inpatient medication stops take effect at the time of discharge order entry.
- Pharmacy must dispense take-home medications with labeled dosages within 45 minutes of the discharge request.
- Central billing must clear all lab, diagnostic, and bed charges within 60 minutes of consultant sign-off.
# Patient Rights, Responsibilities, and Informed Consent Policy
Document ID: POL-ETH-002 | Version: 3.1 | Department: Legal & Clinical Governance
## 1. Patient Rights
- Access to Care: Impartial access to medically indicated treatment regardless of race, creed, gender, or financial status.
- Respect and Dignity: Right to receive respectful, compassionate care and privacy during examinations, consultations, and treatments.
- Health Information: Right to receive full, comprehensible information regarding diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment options.
- Refusal of Treatment: Right to refuse any treatment or procedure and to be informed of the medical consequences of such refusal.
## 2. Informed Consent Protocols
- Standard Procedures: Consent is required prior to all surgical operations, invasive diagnostic procedures, and blood transfusions.
- Requirements for Valid Consent:
1. The physician performing the procedure must personally explain indications, material risks (>1% incidence), alternatives, and consequences of non-treatment.
2. Consent must be obtained when the patient is conscious, alert, and free from sedative influence.
3. Valid for 30 calendar days unless the clinical condition or proposed surgical approach changes.
- Emergency Exception: When immediate intervention is necessary to prevent loss of life or limb and the patient is incapacitated with no legal surrogate available, implied consent applies.

# Clinical Shift Handover Standard Operating Procedure (ISBAR Method)
Document ID: STF-NUR-002 | Version: 2.2 | Department: Nursing Services
## 1. Policy Overview

Bedside shift handovers must occur face-to-face between outgoing and incoming nursing staff at the change of each shift (07:00, 15:00, 23:00). Verbal transfer alone without electronic verification is non-compliant.
## 2. Handover Structure (ISBAR)
- I - Identify: State patient name, age, MRN, bed number, admitting diagnosis, and attending physician.
- S - Situation: Current clinical status, recent surgeries/procedures, and level of stability over the preceding 8 hours.
- B - Background: Relevant medical history, drug allergies, baseline mobility, and cognitive state.
- A - Assessment:
- Last set of vital signs and Early Warning Score (NEWS2).
- IV access sites, infusion lines, patency, and dressing condition.
- Presence of drains, urinary catheters, surgical wounds, and drain outputs.
- R - Recommendation: Pending laboratory/radiology results, medications due in the upcoming shift, planned consults, and specific red flags to watch for.
## 3. Mandatory Safety Checks During Handover
- Verify high-alert infusions against pump programming settings.
- Inspect high-risk skin pressure points (sacrum, heels).
- Check bedside emergency suction and oxygen flow meters.
# Disaster Management and Facility Evacuation Plan
Document ID: EMG-DIS-005 | Version: 1.5 | Department: Facility Safety & Administration
## 1. Emergency Codes
- Code Red: Fire or smoke detection.
- Code Yellow: External mass-casualty disaster/incident.
- Code Orange: Hazardous chemical or biological spill.
- Code Black: Bomb threat or armed intruder.
## 2. Fire Evacuation (R.A.C.E Protocol)
- R - Rescue: Remove any patients or visitors in immediate danger if safe to do so.
- A - Alarm: Activate the manual pull station and call the security control room (Ext: 1111).
- C - Contain: Close all doors and windows behind you to contain fire, smoke, and oxygen feed.
- E - Extinguish/Evacuate: Extinguish small localized fires using P.A.S.S (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep) or proceed with horizontal evacuation.
## 3. Evacuation Tiers
- Horizontal Evacuation (Priority 1): Move patients through fire barrier doors to an adjacent safe zone on the same floor.
- Vertical Evacuation (Priority 2): Utilized only if horizontal zones are breached.
1. Ambulatory patients evacuated first via designated emergency stairwells.
2. Non-ambulatory patients transported via evacuation sleds/sheets (Do not use elevators during Code Red).
3. Ventilator-dependent and ICU patients evacuated last with dedicated transport monitors and portable oxygen cylinders.
# Code Blue and Cardiac Arrest Resuscitation Protocol
Document ID: EMG-RES-001 | Version: 4.0 | Department: Emergency & Critical Care
## 1. Activation Phase
- Any staff member identifying an unresponsive patient who is not breathing or only gasping (and pulseless) must:
1. Call out for local assistance immediately.
2. Press the nearest Code Blue Wall Button or dial internal extension 2222.
3. Announce: "Code Blue, [Building], [Floor], [Room/Bed Number]".
4. Initiate chest compressions immediately (100–120 bpm, 5–6 cm depth).
## 2. First Responder Actions
- Retrieve nearest Crash Cart and automated/manual defibrillator.
- Apply defibrillator pads while continuing compressions.
- Deliver oxygen via Bag-Valve-Mask (BVM) with reservoir at 15 L/min (30:2 ratio or 1 breath every 6 seconds with advanced airway).
## 3. Team Roles Upon Arrival (Within 3 Minutes)
- Team Leader (Senior ER/ICU Physician): Directs code, orders medications, manages rhythm checks, makes termination decisions.
- Airway Manager (Anesthesiologist/Respiratory Therapist): Secures advanced airway, verifies tube placement via waveform capnography.
- Compressor 1 & 2: Alternate chest compressions every 2 minutes (after rhythm analysis) to avoid fatigue.
- Medication/IV Nurse: Establishes IV/IO access, prepares and administers Epinephrine 1 mg IV every 3-5 minutes, logs times.
- Defibrillator Operator: Operates monitor, announces "CLEAR" prior to charging and delivery of shock.
- Recorder: Maintains real-time documentation of interventions, rhythm changes, shocks delivered, and medications.s
# Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (ASP) Policy
Document ID: MED-ASP-004 | Version: 2.0 | Department: Infectious Disease & Pharmacy
## 1. Classification of Antibiotics
- Access Group (First-line): Cefazolin, Amoxicillin, Metronidazole. Usable without prior approval.
- Watch Group (Restricted): Piperacillin-Tazobactam, Vancomycin, Ciprofloxacin. Requires documented indication.
- Reserve Group (Critical): Meropenem, Colistin, Linezolid, Tigecycline.
- Restricted for multi-drug resistant (MDR) pathogens only.
- Requires pre-authorization from the Infectious Disease (ID) Consultant within 24 hours of first dose.
## 2. Blood Culture and Empiric Therapy Rules
- Relevant microbiological cultures (blood, sputum, urine, wound) must be drawn prior to administering the first dose of broad-spectrum antibiotics.
- Time-Out at 48–72 Hours: The primary care team must review culture and sensitivity results at day 3 to either:
1. De-escalate to a targeted, narrower-spectrum agent.
2. Switch from IV to oral formulation if the patient is afebrile and tolerating oral intake.
3. Discontinue antibiotics if an infectious etiology is ruled out.
# Safe Handling and Administration of High-Alert Medications
Document ID: MED-HAM-002 | Version: 3.0 | Department: Pharmacy & Patient Safety
## 1. Definition and Scope
High-alert medications bear a heightened risk of causing significant patient harm when used in error. Classes include:
- Intravenous Potassium Chloride (KCl) concentrates
- Insulin (all formulations)
- Anticoagulants (Heparin, Enoxaparin, Warfarin)
- Opioids and sedatives
- Neuromuscular blocking agents
## 2. Safeguards and Storage Rules
- Concentrated Electrolytes: Potassium Chloride vials >2 mEq/mL are strictly barred from general wards; they must reside exclusively in the central pharmacy and ICU satellite stores.
- Tall-Man Lettering: Systems must display look-alike/sound-alike drugs as:
- DOPamine vs. DOBUTamine
- predniSONE vs. prednisoLONE
- hydrOXYzine vs. hydrALAZINE
## 3. Independent Double-Check Protocol
- Two licensed registered nurses must independently verify:
1. Patient identification band (name and MRN).
2. Physician prescription order.
3. Drug calculation, vial concentration, and total volume drawn.
4. Infusion pump settings (rate, volume to be infused, channel assignment).
- Both nurses must sign the Medication Administration Record (MAR) prior to delivery.

# Hospital Department Directory, Floor Maps, and Operating Hours
Document ID: OPS-DIR-001 | Version: 4.1 | Department: Facility Operations
## Main Hospital Complex Layout
### Basement Level (B1)
- Diagnostic Imaging: MRI, 128-Slice CT Scan, Fluoroscopy (Open 24/7).
- Central Sterile Services Department (CSSD).
- Hospital Inpatient Pharmacy & Bulk Store.
- Mortuary.
### Ground Floor (Level 0)
- Emergency Department (ED) & Urgent Care Unit (Open 24/7).
- Main Reception, Patient Registration, and Admission Desks.
- Outpatient Department (OPD) Clinics 1 to 24 (08:00 AM – 08:00 PM).
- Phlebotomy & Sample Collection Center (07:00 AM – 09:00 PM).
- Emergency Pharmacy (Open 24/7).
### First Floor (Level 1)
- Main Operating Theater Complex (OT 1 to OT 8).
- Surgical Intensive Care Unit (SICU) - 16 Beds.
- Day Surgery Ward & Post-Anesthesia Care Unit (PACU).
- Endoscopy & Colonoscopy Suite.
### Second Floor (Level 2)
- Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU) - 20 Beds.
- Coronary Care Unit (CCU) & Cardiac Catheterization Lab (Cath Lab).
- Neonatal ICU (NICU) & Pediatric ICU (PICU).
- Labor and Delivery Suites.
### Third to Fifth Floors (Levels 3 - 5)
- Level 3: General Inpatient Wards (Medical & Surgical).
- Level 4: Semi-Private and Private Inpatient Rooms (401 - 440).
- Level 5: Executive Inpatient Suites (501 - 515), Administration & HR Offices.
